headline: National Zoological Park marks World Rhino Day with First Eco-Club Teachers’ Orientation to strengthen School Outreach
fullText:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

National Zoological Park marks World Rhino Day with First Eco-Club Teachers’ Orientation to strengthen School Outreach

22 SEP 2026 10:05PM by PIB Delhi

The National Zoological Park (NZP), New Delhi, observed World Rhino Day 2026 today with a series of awareness and educational programmes aimed at promoting rhino conservation and strengthening public and school engagement in wildlife and biodiversity conservation.

As part of its school outreach initiative, the Zoo organised its first orientation programme for eco-club in-charge teachers. Teachers from 12 schools of Delhi participated in the programme. The Director (NZP) interacted with the teachers and highlighted the importance of strengthening collaboration between the Zoo and schools for environmental education and conservation awareness.

The orientation familiarised teachers with the Zoo’s environmental education initiatives, nature-based educational activities, citizen science initiatives and other outreach programmes. It also envisaged greater participation of schools in workshops, awareness programmes and competitions organised on important eco days and other relevant occasions.

A doodle activity and public awareness talk was subsequently organised for visitors at the Zoo’s exit gate. Zoo staff interacted with visitors and shared information on rhinoceros, their ecological significance, conservation status and the challenges faced by rhino populations in the wild. The programmes witnessed enthusiastic participation from school teachers and visitors and provided an important platform to enhance awareness about rhino conservation, wildlife protection and the need to conserve biodiversity.

A special keepers’ talk on rhinos was also organised at the rhino enclosures. Zoo keepers interacted with visitors and provided insights into rhino behaviour, feeding habits, daily care and scientific management at the National Zoological Park. At present, the National Zoological Park, New Delhi, has one adult female rhinoceros, named Anjuha, in its collection.

headline: Rashtriya Poshan Maah 2026: Lecture on Dietary Diversity and Adequate Protein Organised at MDNIY
fullText:
Rashtriya Poshan Maah 2026: Lecture on Dietary Diversity and Adequate Protein Organised at MDNIY

23 SEP 2026 4:08PM by PIB Delhi

Morarji Desai National Institute of Yoga (MDNIY), Ministry of Ayush, organised the inaugural programme of the 9th Rashtriya Poshan Maah 2026, highlighting the importance of dietary diversity, healthy eating practices and adequate protein intake. Organised under the aegis of the Ministry of Women and Child Development, Government of India, the programme focused on informed dietary choices and adequate nutrition.

A nutrition pledge was administered during the programme under the leadership of Dr. Jyoti Keswani, Director (Additional Charge), MDNIY and Chief Patron of the event. Dr. Keswani highlighted the importance of greater public awareness about nutritious dietary practices and healthy lifestyles.

An expert lecture on “Dietary Diversity and Adequate Protein” was delivered by Dr. Swati Jain, Scientist ‘D’, ICMR-National Institute of Cancer Prevention and Research (ICMR-NICPR). She emphasised that protein adequacy should be considered as part of a balanced and diverse diet.

Dr. Jain highlighted the role of protein in tissue repair, immunity, muscle maintenance and the production of enzymes and hormones. Referring to the ICMR-NIN Nutrient Requirements for Indians, she noted that the safe protein allowance for healthy adults is 0.83 g per kg body weight per day when the diet contains high-quality protein, and 1.0 g per kg per day for predominantly cereal-based diets with lower protein quality. She also noted that protein requirements vary with age, body size, physiological state, physical activity and health status.

Emphasising dietary diversity, Dr. Jain encouraged inclusion of pulses, dairy, soy, nuts and seeds along with cereals. She cited traditional food combinations such as dal-rice, roti-chana, idli-sambar, dosa-sambar and khichdi as practical examples of complementary protein sources. She also highlighted affordable protein-containing foods such as sattu, dal, roasted chana, peanuts and soy.

Dr. Jain noted that protein intake should be distributed across meals rather than concentrated in a single meal. For individuals practising Yoga, she emphasised that overall daily protein intake and a balanced diet are more important than focusing exclusively on a post-exercise “protein window”.

The programme was coordinated by Dr. Khushbu Jain, Assistant Professor (Biochemistry), MDNIY, and conducted by Dr. Pawan Kumar, Assistant Professor (Yoga Education).

The event was attended by Md. Taiyab Alam, Communication and Documentation Officer and Deputy Director (I/C), MDNIY; Dr. I. N. Acharya, Programme Officer (Yoga Therapy); faculty members, students, officers and staff of the Institute.

As part of the month-long observance, MDNIY will organise a series of awareness, educational and outreach activities, including a nutrition quiz, poster-making competition, nutrition awareness programme for school children, and a community outreach programme on maternal nutrition and Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY). The observance will conclude with a Valedictory Programme on 8 October 2026, featuring a poster exhibition, recognition of participants and an awareness session on Ayurvedic nutrition and healthy dietary practices.

headline: CARA organises adoption awareness workshop in Manipur to combat Illegal adoption
fullText:
Ministry of Women and Child Development

CARA organises adoption awareness workshop in Manipur to combat Illegal adoption

Workshop held under the theme “Legal Adoption. Safe Childhood. Secure Future. Say No to Illegal Adoption”

Around 150 stakeholders sensitised on legal, safe and child-centric adoption practices

23 SEP 2026 4:01PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Adoption Resource Authority (CARA), under the aegis of the Ministry of Women and Child Development, Government of India, organised an Adoption Awareness Workshop at North A.O.C., Imphal, Manipur on 23rd September 2026, under the theme “Legal Adoption. Safe Childhood. Secure Future. Say No to Illegal Adoption!”. The workshop was organised in collaboration with the Department of Social Welfare, Government of Manipur, and Manipur State Adoption Resource Agency (SARA).

The workshop was held in the presence of Shri Sheikh Abdul Hakim, Director, Social Welfare Department, Manipur; Smt. K. Sunderbala, Addl. SP (IUCAW), Imphal West; Smt. Rupanshi Pandey, Assistant Director, CARA; Smt. Ankita Bharadwaj, Assistant Director, CARA, along with senior officials and stakeholders from the child protection and adoption ecosystem. The workshop brought together around 150 participants to strengthen awareness about the legal, transparent and child-centric adoption process and to highlight the risks and consequences associated with illegal adoption practices.

The workshop brought together representatives from the Department of Social Welfare, CWCs, DCPUs, SAAs, CCIs, Health and Police Departments, Judiciary, Legal Services Authorities, hospitals and private nursing homes, ASHA and ANM workers, civil society organisations and media, among others.

Addressing the participants, Shri Sheikh Abdul Hakim, Director, Social Welfare Department, Manipur, emphasised the importance of coordinated efforts by all stakeholders to ensure that children are protected from unregulated and illegal adoption arrangements.Smt. Rupanshi Pandey, Assistant Director, CARA, highlighted the need for vigilance and coordinated action at every level, stating, “Preventing illegal adoption requires vigilance and coordinated action at every level.”

As part of an interactive component, participants were divided into four groups comprising Police & Anti-Human Trafficking Units (AHTUs); CMOs, hospitals/private nursing homes, ANMs & Anganwadi Workers; Legal/Judiciary & CWCs; and SARA, DCPOs, SAAs/CCIs and other stakeholders. The group discussions provided a platform for participants to reflect on their existing understanding of the legal adoption framework, identify gaps in awareness and coordination, and put forward practical suggestions for strengthening prevention, identification, reporting and response mechanisms.

Each group subsequently presented its key observations and recommendations, highlighting the importance of inter-departmental coordination, timely information sharing, responsible referral and strict compliance with the statutory adoption process.

A special real-life experience-sharing session by Shri Thingnam Roshan Singh, Manager/Coordinator, SAA, Imphal, provided practical insights into addressing suspected cases of illegal adoption. The session highlighted the importance of timely intervention and the role of field-level child protection functionaries in safeguarding children.

A fiction film on legal adoption was also presented to reinforce the importance of following the authorised adoption process and create greater awareness about the risks associated with illegal adoption. The workshop also featured a child-centric performance by children of State Bal Bhavan, promoting the message of family-based care and the importance of providing children with safe, nurturing and supportive family environments. The short play connected with the audience and reinforced the workshop’s child-focused message.

The Manipur workshop reinforced the need for continuous awareness, stronger coordination and timely intervention across the child protection and adoption ecosystem. Participants were sensitised to their respective responsibilities and the importance of ensuring that every child requiring care and protection is dealt with strictly in accordance with law and with the best interests of the child as the paramount consideration.

The workshop concluded with a renewed collective commitment to strengthen vigilance, improve coordination among stakeholders and promote only legal, safe and child-centric adoption practices in Manipur.

headline: Press Note on Domestic Tourism Expenditure Survey July 2025 to June 2026
fullText:
Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation

Press Note on Domestic Tourism Expenditure Survey July 2025 to June 2026

23 SEP 2026 4:00PM by PIB Delhi

Social visits lead domestic trips

Business Trips record highest spending

Pilgrimage & Religious emerges as top purpose

Snapshot: Around 48 trips out of 100 overnight trips were performed for ‘pilgrimage & religious’ purpose followed by 30 trips for ‘health & medical’ purpose for overnight trips completed during the last 365 days. On average, out of 100 overnight trips completed during the last 30 days, 89 trips were performed for ‘social’ purpose. ‘Business trips’ recorded the maximum average expenditure per trip of Rs. 5,949 by households for overnight trips made during the last 30 days. ‘Social’ (33%) and ‘Shopping’ (26%) were the two most frequently undertaken same-day trips by households, with shopping accounting for the highest expenditure share in both rural and urban areas.

The Domestic Tourism Expenditure Survey (DTES), conducted by the National Statistics Office (NSO), mainly captures the details of domestic overnight trips like duration of trip, mode of transport, type of stay availed, trip expenses etc. Additionally, some information is also collected on domestic same-day trips and expenditure incurred on them.

The present survey was conducted during July, 2025 to June, 2026 as a part of NSS 80th round. The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) has released the findings of this survey through a report titled ‘Domestic Tourism in India’.

Data for this survey were collected for (i) domestic overnight trips completed during last 365 days with leading purposes holidaying, leisure and recreation; pilgrimage & religious; health & medical and shopping, (ii) domestic overnight trips completed during last 30 days with leading purposes business, social, education & training and others and (iii) same day trips completed during last 30 days.

A brief account of the survey in terms of coverage, sample design etc. along with glossary of terms is provided in the endnote.

B1. Domestic overnight trips completed during last 365 days with leading purposes holidaying, leisure and recreation; pilgrimage & religious; health & medical and shopping:

Number of overnight trips generated per 100 households reporting at least one overnight trip (tourist household) during last 365 days was - 127 per 100 rural tourist households (118 per 100 rural tourist households in 2014-15) and 132 per 100 urban tourist households (121 per 100 urban tourist households in 2014-15).

Highest share of trips was reported for 'pilgrimage & religious' purpose (48%) by both sectors.

The second-largest share in overnight trips was for ‘health & medical’ purposes in rural areas (38.4%) and ‘holidaying, leisure & recreation’ in urban areas (36.4%).

Average trip size was recorded as 2.03 overnight visitors per trip. Around 80% of visitors preferred to stay for 5 days or less during their respective overnight trips.

May and October were the peak months for domestic overnight trips undertaken for holidaying, leisure & recreation purpose during the last 365 days.

For rural households, bus was the dominant mode of travel with 32% share in the visitor-trips while train (35%) was the most availed mode for travelling by urban households for such trips.

Among urban overnight visitors, hotels and guesthouses were the most preferred type of stay, accounting for 36% share in visitor-trips. In rural areas, other non-commercial stays accounted for the largest share (28%) which included stays in one’s own vacation home (second home), temporary accommodation provided by employers, accommodation provided by religious or missionary organisations free of charge, etc.

Combining visitors both from within the state and from other states, Uttar Pradesh accounted for the highest share in total visitor-trips (15.7%), followed by Tamil Nadu (13.4%) and Rajasthan (8.0%).

Health & medical trips incurred maximum expenditure (including both package & non-package components) in both rural (Rs. 29,454) and urban (Rs. 41,649) areas among all the trips completed during the reference period.

Highest share of expenditure was reported on ‘transport’ component for overnight trips performed with the leading purpose ‘holidaying, leisure and recreation’.

B2 Domestic overnight trips completed during last 30 days with leading purposes business, social, education & training and others:

Number of overnight trips generated per 100 households reporting at least one overnight trip (tourist household) during last 30 days was - 113 per 100 rural tourist households and 111 per 100 urban tourist households.

Trips made for leading purpose ‘social’ accounted for the maximum share of 89% among all such trips.

Average trip size reported was 1.95 overnight visitors per trip, while average trip duration for around 45% of visitor-trips was 2-3 days.

Bus was the most preferred mode of travel having 48% & 44% share in visitor-trips in rural and urban areas respectively.

Both for rural and urban households, friend & relatives place was the major type of stay.

Combining visitors both from within the state and from other states, Uttar Pradesh registered highest share of visitor-trips (15.5%) as state of main destination for such trips followed by Bihar (10.5%) and Tamil Nadu (9.6%).

For the trips completed during last 30 days, both rural (Rs. 5,179) and urban (Rs. 6,934) households spent the most on overnight trips with leading purpose business.

B3. Same-day trips completed during last 30 days:

In rural areas, 65.1% (57.1 % in 2014-15) households and 46.2% (40.6% in 2014-15) households in urban areas undertook at least one same-day trip during last 30 days.

Number of overnight trips generated per 100 households reporting at least one same-day trip (tourist household) during last 30 days was - 185 per 100 rural tourist households and 156 per 100 urban tourist households.

Same-day trips with leading purposes ‘social (rural-32%, urban-37%)’ and ‘shopping (rural-29%, urban-17%)’ were the two most frequently undertaken same-day trips by both rural and urban households.

Highest expenditure was observed for same-day trips with leading purpose ‘shopping’ followed by ‘health & medical trips’ in both rural and urban areas.

Maximum share of expenditure was reported on ‘shopping’ component among all same-day trips performed by both rural (51%) and urban (41%) households.

Endnote: A brief about the geographical coverage, sample size, sample design, reference periods for the Domestic Tourism Expenditure Survey

A. Geographical coverage

This survey covered the whole of the Indian Union, except the villages in Andaman and Nicobar Islands which remain difficult to access throughout the year.

A total of 24,778 FSUs were surveyed at all-India level consisting of 14,371 rural and 10,407 urban FSUs for this survey. The number of households surveyed was 2,46,113 (1,42,603 in rural areas and 1,03,510 in urban areas).

C. Sample design

A multi-stage stratified sampling design was used for this survey, where villages/urban blocks or Sub-Units (SUs) of these were regarded as the First Stage Units (FSU) and the households as the Ultimate Stage Units (USU). Both the FSUs and USUs were selected with Simple Random Sampling Without Replacement (SRSWOR).

D. Data Collection Mechanism:

The data for Domestic Tourism Expenditure Survey of NSS 80th round was collected through Schedule 21.1. The data for the survey were collected in tablet using Computer Assisted Personal Interviewing (CAPI).

E. Glossary of terms used:

overnight trip | It refers to the movement to a main destination- for a duration of not less than twelve hours (including 12:00 midnight to 5:00 A.M.) in two consecutive calendar days (i.e. crossing midnight or 00:00 hours) and of not more than 180 days - by one or more household members outside their usual environment (which included their usual place of residence (UPR)) and return to the same UPR (a round trip), irrespective of place of stay during this period.

domestic visitor | A visitor is a person (household member), residing in the country, who performed an overnight or same-day trip.

leading purpose | The leading purpose of a trip is that purpose without which none of the household members in that trip would have undertaken the trip. Leading purpose of a trip is unique to all the members participating in that trip.

same-day trip | A same-day trip is the one that does not involve an overnight stay (i.e. duration of more than 12 hrs and incl. 12:00 midnight to 05:00 A.M.) but fulfills other conditions of overnight trips, irrespective of the number of hours spent on the trip. It may be either completed on the same calendar date or spread over two consecutive calendar dates.

F. Detailed Survey Report:

For detailed understanding of the objectives, coverage, concepts & definitions, methodology and major findings from this survey, the NSS Report No.597 ‘Domestic Tourism in India’ published by NSO, MoSPI may be referred, which is available on the website of ministry (https://www.mospi.gov.in).

Scan QR code to access MoSPI Publications/ Reports

(Release ID: 2313894)

headline: 11th Ayurveda Day Celebrated Across India and the World; Grand National Celebration Held in Nagpur
fullText:
11th Ayurveda Day Celebrated Across India and the World; Grand National Celebration Held in Nagpur

Ayurveda Day Celebration Highlights Evidence-Based Research, Innovation and Healthy Living

Ayurveda's journey from tradition to evidence to innovation will secure health of future generations: PM Shri Narendra Modi

Union Minister Shri Prataprao Jadhav calls for making healthy lifestyle and preventive healthcare a people’s movement

Knowledge, Evidence and Innovation Will Shape the Future of Ayurveda: Ayush Secretary, Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha

11th Ayurveda Day Witnesses Launch of Safety Dossiers, Standard Treatment Guidelines, Ayush Services Sector Report, Ayush Vision 2030 and CCRAS–AGNI Portal

Scientific Sessions Highlight Ayurveda’s Role in Future Healthcare, Public Health and Addressing the Burden of Non-Communicable Diseases

23 SEP 2026 3:48PM by PIB Delhi

The 11th Ayurveda Day was celebrated with enthusiasm across India and the world. The grand national celebrations were held in Nagpur, Maharashtra. This year’s theme was “Ayurveda for a Healthier Tomorrow (स्वस्थ भविष्य के लिए आयुर्वेद)”. The programme witnessed the unveiling of key reports and documents, including the report on the Ayush Services Sector and “Ayush Vision 2030”, along with the launch of the CCRAS–AGNI Web Portal. The event also featured scientific sessions on Ayurveda’s role in healthcare and public health, as well as the roadmap towards 2047.

Hon'ble Prime Minister’s message on the occasion was read out during the programme. In his message, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi said that Ayurveda’s journey from tradition to knowledge, evidence and innovation will contribute to securing the health and wellbeing of future generations. He highlighted that Ayurveda’s identity has expanded beyond India’s borders, with the AYUSH Visa facility enabling foreign nationals to seek treatment under AYUSH systems in India. Referring to the resolve of ‘Shakti ki Sadhna’, the Prime Minister said that India is moving steadily towards a Viksit Bharat and expressed confidence that institutions, experts and youth associated with Ayurveda will take this rich tradition to new heights and contribute to building a healthy, capable and strong nation.

The celebration ceremony was virtually inaugurated by Union Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Ayush and Minister of State, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Shri Prataprao Jadhav in the presence of Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha; Director General, Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS), Prof. (Vaidya) Rabinarayan Acharya, and other dignitaries.

Addressing the celebration, Union Minister Shri Prataprao Jadhav described Ayurveda as a key part of India's health vision, saying, "स्वास्थ्य का पहला केंद्र अस्पताल नहीं, हमारा घर है। स्वास्थ्य का पहला आधार दवा नहीं, हमारी जीवनशैली है।" Citing the principle "स्वस्थस्य स्वास्थ्य रक्षणम्, आतुरस्य विकार प्रशमनम्", he said Ayurveda prioritises preserving health alongside treatment, an approach he called increasingly relevant amid rising lifestyle-related health concerns.

Shri Prataprao Jadhav cited the WHO Global Traditional Medicine Centre in Jamnagar, ITRA Jamnagar's recognition as an Institute of National Importance, and the inclusion of Ayurveda, Siddha and Unani in the WHO ICD-11 classification as key steps in internationalising traditional medicine. He called for connecting tradition with knowledge, evidence and innovation, adding that Ayurveda Day should extend beyond an annual observance to drive wider public engagement on healthy living.

Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, emphasised that the future of Ayurveda lies in connecting its knowledge tradition with scientific evidence, innovation and public health outcomes. He stressed the need to strengthen research, quality, safety and standardisation while promoting collaboration between Ayurveda and other healthcare systems. Highlighting key developments including the WHO Global Traditional Medicine Centre in Jamnagar, more than 43,000 research publications on the Ayush Research Portal, over 200 BIS standards and the Ayush Quality Mark, he said these efforts are aimed at making Ayush systems more scientific, evidence-based and globally relevant.

The programme witnessed the launch of Safety Dossiers on Gokshura (Tribulus terrestris) and Chandrasura (Lepidium sativum), Standard Treatment Guidelines (STGs) on Skin Disorders, and the first-ever Report on the “Ayush Services Sector”, prepared by the Research and Information System for Developing Countries (RIS), providing an assessment of the Ayush services sector.

The event also saw the launch of “From Traditional Wisdom to Global Leadership: Ayush Vision 2030”, the Status Report on Ayush-related Inventions in India, and the CCRAS–AGNI Assessment Scale Web Portal. The initiatives focus on strengthening research, documentation, innovation, clinical guidance and the systematic translation of Ayurveda knowledge into practice.

The programme also featured the presentation of Ayush Quality Mark Certification to four eligible industries by the Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, reflecting the emphasis on quality and standardisation within the Ayush sector.

The celebrations featured two scientific sessions on the evolving role of Ayurveda in healthcare and public health. The first session, “Shashwatam to Vishwas – Ayurveda for a Healthier Tomorrow and the Road to 2047”, featured Dr. G. Geethakrishnan Pillai, Unit Head, WHO Global Traditional Medicine Centre, Jamnagar, and focused on the future trajectory of Ayurveda, evidence generation and its role in the broader health vision towards 2047. The second session, “Integrating Therapies is needed to reduce NCD Burden by 2027”, featured Dr. Shiv Kumar Sarin, Director, Institute of Liver and Biliary Sciences (ILBS), New Delhi, and deliberated on the potential of integrated therapeutic approaches in addressing the growing burden of non-communicable diseases.

The scientific deliberations were followed by a summary presented by Prof. Sanjeev Sharma, Vice Chancellor, National Institute of Ayurveda, Jaipur. Prof. (Dr.) Unnat P. Pandit, Controller General of Patents, Designs & Trade Marks, also delivered remarks on the report on Ayush-related Inventions in India, while Dr. A. Raghu, Adviser (Ayurveda), Ministry of Ayush, spoke on the Standard Treatment Guidelines on Skin Disorders.

The event was graced by Shri Satyajit Paul, Senior Statistical Advisor, Ministry of Ayush; and Prof. Sachin Kumar Sharma, Director General, Research and Information System for Developing Countries (RIS) along with senior officials of the Ministry of Ayush, representatives of Ayush Councils and institutions.

A National Medicinal Plants Exhibition was also set up at the venue, featuring stalls by national institutions under the Ministry of Ayush and attracting considerable interest among visitors and participants.

The national celebration in Nagpur brought together practitioners, researchers, scientists, academics, institutions and other stakeholders from across the country, highlighting the growing focus on evidence, research, innovation, quality and holistic care in advancing Ayurveda.

(Release ID: 2313893)
summaryText:
### OVERVIEW
The 11th Ayurveda Day was celebrated globally, with the grand national ceremony held in Nagpur, Maharashtra, under the theme "Ayurveda for a Healthier Tomorrow." The event focused on advancing evidence-based research, innovation, and quality standardization, while launching key strategic documents like the Ayush Vision 2030 and safety guidelines to integrate Ayurveda into future healthcare and public health systems.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS

headline: India Shares Experience in Digitisation and Modernisation of Land Records with Sri Lankan Delegation
fullText:
Ministry of Rural Development

India Shares Experience in Digitisation and Modernisation of Land Records with Sri Lankan Delegation

23 SEP 2026 3:30PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Land Resources (DoLR), Ministry of Rural Development, today hosted a delegation of civil servants from Sri Lanka visiting India under an exposure programme coordinated by the National Centre for Good Governance (NCGG). The interaction was held under the chairpersonship of Shri P. Narahari, Joint Secretary, Department of Land Resources, and focused on India’s experience in digitising and modernising land records, with emphasis on the Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme (DILRMP), computerisation of Records of Rights (RoRs), integration of registration with land records and the Unique Land Parcel Identification Number (ULPIN).

The Sri Lankan delegation was led by Ms. Pathirage Laxman Pathmakumari, Team Leader of the Delegation, Sri Lanka, and included Dr. Mukesh K. Bhandari, Course Coordinator, National Centre for Good Governance, LBSNAA, and Dr. A.P. Singh, Course Director, along with senior officials from Sri Lanka’s land, survey and administrative services.

Welcoming the delegation, Shri P. Narahari highlighted the close ties between India and Sri Lanka and the importance of sharing experiences in public administration. He said, “Land is not merely an administrative record; it is closely linked to livelihoods, economic activity, access to government benefits and citizens’ sense of security. India’s experience has been one of continuously modernising land administration through technology, while recognising the diversity of our States and their land systems. We are pleased to share these experiences with our Sri Lankan colleagues and equally look forward to learning from their institutional practices and reforms.”

During the interaction, Shri Amit Kumar Singh, Director (LR), DoLR, presented an overview of the macro reforms and technological framework powering DILRMP. He highlighted India’s transition from conventional paper-based records to integrated digital land information systems.

Shri Amit Kumar Singh said, “The transformation of land records is not merely about converting paper records into digital form. The larger objective is to create an integrated land information ecosystem where textual records, spatial information, registration data and geospatial technologies complement each other.”

Key DILRMP milestones shared with the delegation included:

99.90% of textual Records of Rights (RoRs) computerised.

97.43% of cadastral maps digitised and 76.16% of land parcels fully georeferenced.

85.24% spatial-textual integration achieved between cadastral maps and RoRs.

40.58 crore+ land parcels assigned the 14-digit alphanumeric Bhu-Aadhaar (ULPIN).

98.96% of Sub-Registrar Offices (SROs) computerised.

17 States/UTs adopting the centralised National Generic Document Registration System (NGDRS), while 17 States operate state-specific digital registration software.

94.11% of Revenue Courts computerised under the Revenue Court Case Management System (RCCMS), enabling real-time litigation marking on property records.

The delegation was also briefed on the integration of cadastral maps and Records of Rights to ensure consistency in ownership details, parcel boundaries and area information.

The interaction covered the integration of property registration with land records through mutation, including ongoing reforms towards paperless registration and automated mutation. Under the emerging system, registration information can be electronically transmitted to the concerned revenue authority for updating land records, reducing delays and the need for repeated visits to government offices.

The delegation was also given a walkthrough of the Bharat Land Stack, an integrated, GIS-based federated architecture bringing together satellite and drone imagery, georeferenced cadastral boundaries, Records of Rights, property registration data, master planning and zoning regulations, building approvals, restrictions and litigation, circle rates and tenancy details. The architecture seeks to provide an integrated digital view of land-related information associated with a parcel.

The visiting officials were further briefed on ULPIN, or Bhu-Aadhaar, which assigns a unique 14-digit alphanumeric identity to land parcels based on their geospatial coordinates. The system facilitates linkage of land parcels with other land-related datasets and maintains linkages when parcels undergo subdivision.

Shri Sarvadanand Barnwal, Director (LR), DoLR, presented a comprehensive overview of the NAKSHA (National Geospatial Knowledge-based Land Survey of Urban Habitations) programme and its approach to modernising urban land records through advanced surveying and geospatial technologies.

The presentation detailed the end-to-end NAKSHA workflow, including:

Deployment of 2D Nadir cameras, 5-camera Oblique systems and LiDAR sensors mounted on aerial drones for centimetre-level positional accuracy.

Generation of Ortho-Rectified Imagery (ORI), Digital Elevation Models (DEM) and 3D Reality Models for complex urban landscapes.

RTK GNSS rover-based ground truthing, participatory ground validation and transparent claims and objections redressal.

Aerial flying completed across 145 of 150 Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) under the pilot phase, progressing towards issuance of legally authentic Urban Property (UrPro) Cards.

Shri Sarvadanand Barnwal said, “NAKSHA is an important step towards strengthening urban land governance through modern geospatial technologies. By creating reliable and integrated urban land records, the programme can support better land administration, improve planning and contribute to greater ease of living for citizens.”

The interaction provided the Sri Lankan delegation with an overview of India’s experience in large-scale land governance reforms, spanning digitisation of land records, spatial-textual integration, digital registration, mutation, geospatial identification of land parcels, computerisation of Revenue Courts and modern urban land mapping.

The engagement underscored the importance of international knowledge-sharing in public administration and highlighted how digital and geospatial technologies can support transparent, integrated and citizen-centric land governance and improve public service delivery.

headline: Academia Industry collaboration traced the mechanism of how preservatives take down bacteria enabling smarter preservation
fullText:
Ministry of Science & Technology

Academia Industry collaboration traced the mechanism of how preservatives take down bacteria enabling smarter preservation

23 SEP 2026 3:17PM by PIB Delhi

Scientists have captured, for the first time, the moment of bacteria succumbing to preservative attack. Using advanced imaging and chemical analysis, the team revealed how preservatives disrupt bacterial cells from within. The breakthrough opens the door to designing smarter and safer preservation technologies across home and personal care categories.

Both Sodium benzoate (SB) and Phenoxyethanol (POE) are effective preservatives. Sodium benzoate (SB) has been keeping foods such as pickles, ketchup and fizzy drinks safe since the early 1900s, being the very first food preservative approved by the US FDA, back in 1908. Phenoxyethanol (POE) is the newer addition, having been used in shampoo, moisturiser, sunscreen and even certain vaccines for decades. Despite more than a century of widespread use, the molecular mechanisms underlying the anti-bacterial activity of these two lead preservatives, SB and POE, remain poorly understood.

Researchers at Institute of Nano Science & Technology (INST) Mohali, an autonomous institute of the Department of Science and Technology, in collaboration with Unilever R&D Bangalore, addressed this knowledge gap by integrating transmission electron microscopy (TEM) with complementary biochemical analyses to elucidate the antimicrobial mode of action of preservative systems. The study investigated preservative-induced cellular and biochemical responses in two representative bacterial pathogens: the Gram-positive Staphylococcus aureus and the Gram-negative Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

Fig 1: The study revealed a dual mode of action: preservatives compromise the bacterial cell envelope while triggering internal biochemical damage, delivering a coordinated attack on multiple cellular targets.

The researchers found that preservatives attack bacteria on multiple fronts. The microbial cell envelope becomes physically compromised, while reactive aldehydes and oxygen-derived species accumulate inside the cell, disrupting essential proteins, genetic material, and other critical cellular functions. Rather than a single mode of action, the preservatives deliver a coordinated multi-target assault, providing one of the clearest views yet of how bacterial cells are inactivated.

Advanced imaging revealed that sodium benzoate and phenoxyethanol follow distinct pathways to bacterial inactivation. Sodium benzoate induced cellular shrinkage and collapse, whereas phenoxyethanol caused membrane expansion and eventual rupture. The researchers further showed that sodium benzoate becomes significantly more potent in acidic environments, exhibiting an approximately sixteen-fold increase in activity, while phenoxyethanol displayed consistent efficacy across a wide pH range. These findings provide important insights into how preservative performance can be optimized for different formulation conditions.

The team consisting of Ishani Sharma, S M Rose, Madhu Lata, Somnath Das, Nagaraja IS Acharya, Maheshwara Naik, Samiran Mahapatra and Sharmistha Sinha ran bacteria through a gauntlet of tests like inhibition zone and MIC assays to see how much preservative it takes to knock growth down, electron microscopy to literally watch cell shape fall apart, a dye leakage test to catch membranes springing leaks, and two biochemical assays (MBTH and DCFDA) to measure the internal chemical chaos, across two very different bacteria, and both neutral and acidic conditions. Together, these methods helped the researchers connect what a bacterium looks like on the outside to what's actually going wrong on the inside, at the same moment. It was published in the journal: Letters in Applied Microbiology

Fig 2: TEM images: Non-treated cells (P. aeruginosa-top and S. aureus-bottom) vs. cells treated with SB or POE, showing membrane rupture and cytoplasmic leakage (indicated with red arrow).

Knowing exactly how these preservatives work can help industry chose the correct one for a particular product format, (sodium benzoate is suitable for anything acidic and phenoxyethanol is suitable for cases where pH swings shouldn't matter), use just the right amount instead of guessing, cut down on spoilage and waste, and stay a step ahead of bacteria that might otherwise evolve resistance.

headline: From a Village Dream to a Career in Research
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

From a Village Dream to a Career in Research

NFSC Support Enabled Sagar Kodi to Complete His Ph.D. and Build a Promising Academic Career

23 SEP 2026 3:05PM by PIB Delhi

For Sagar Kodi, a 30-year-old scholar belonging to the Scheduled Caste community, pursuing higher education was not merely a personal ambition. It was a path towards supporting his family and contributing to his community.

Coming from a village, Sagar faced financial and geographical barriers in accessing quality higher education. After completing his master's degree, he attempted to qualify for the UGC-NET Junior Research Fellowship but missed the qualifying mark by less than two per cent.

Determined to continue his academic journey, he enrolled in a Ph.D. programme with financial assistance from the university. However, the limited support was insufficient to meet his research expenses and help his family.

At the same time, his family expected him to begin earning and contribute financially after completing his master's degree. These circumstances made it increasingly difficult for Sagar to continue his doctoral research.

Receiving assistance under the National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students proved a turning point in his life. He was supported through both the Junior Research Fellowship and Senior Research Fellowship from 27 December 2019 to 15 May 2024. The last fellowship support received by him amounted to Rs. 42,000.

The fellowship enabled Sagar to pursue his Ph.D. without the constant burden of financial uncertainty. It helped him meet his academic and research expenses while also contributing towards his family's needs. According to him, without support under the scheme, his family's financial circumstances might have prevented him from continuing his doctoral studies.

With determination and timely institutional support, Sagar completed his Ph.D. and established a career in research. He is presently working as a Research Associate at the Anthropological Survey of India, Mysore, with a basic pay of Rs. 37,600 under Level 6.

Sagar's journey demonstrates how targeted fellowship support can enable talented students from disadvantaged communities to overcome financial and geographical barriers, pursue advanced education and build meaningful careers. His achievement has strengthened his family's financial position and placed him in a position to inspire and support others from his community.

Extending gratitude to NFSC, Sagar Kodi said, “The NFSC fellowship enabled me to pursue my Ph.D. without financial hardship and helped me support my family while working towards my academic goals."

Sagar Kodi's story is one of perseverance, aspiration and empowerment a journey that began in a village and led to a promising career in research.

headline: MY Bharat Crosses Landmark Milestone of 3 Crore + Registered Youth in less than 3 Years
fullText:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports

MY Bharat Crosses Landmark Milestone of 3 Crore + Registered Youth in less than 3 Years

Milestone reflects growing participation of young Indians in opportunities for leadership, experiential learning, volunteering and nation-building

23 SEP 2026 3:00PM by PIB Delhi

Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat) (mybharat.gov.in/), the national youth engagement platform of the Department of Youth Affairs, Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports, has crossed the landmark milestone of 3 crore + registered youth. The achievement marks a significant expansion of India's largest youth engagement ecosystem, providing young people with opportunities to participate in experiential learning, volunteering, leadership, civic engagement and youth-led initiatives.

Launched by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on 31 October 2023, MY Bharat was established with the vision of creating a technology-enabled platform through which young Indians can participate in the nation's development journey. At the launch, the Prime Minister emphasised the importance of bringing the country's youth together on a common platform and enabling their greater participation in nation-building. The platform was conceived as an important institutional mechanism for translating the energy, aspirations and potential of India's youth into meaningful participation towards Viksit Bharat @2047.

The journey of MY Bharat has witnessed rapid expansion since its launch. The platform crossed 2 crore + registrations in October 2025 and subsequently expanded its reach to more than 2.46 crore + registered youth by August 2026. The crossing of the 3 crore + mark within the next phase of its expansion reflects the continuing growth of youth participation on the platform.

MY Bharat today serves as a common digital gateway through which young people can discover and participate in Experiential Learning Programmes, volunteering opportunities, quizzes, leadership initiatives, youth dialogues and community engagement activities. As of August 2026, more than 1.22 lakh youth had enrolled in nearly 25,000 Experiential Learning Programmes, providing opportunities for young people to gain practical exposure through participation beyond conventional classroom settings.

The platform has also continued to evolve technologically. An AI-enabled CV Builder has been introduced to help young people create professional profiles, while the platform is being strengthened through digital services and wider grassroots access..

A key initiative being driven through MY Bharat is the Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue (VBYLD) 2027, which is providing young Indians with multiple pathways to showcase their ideas, creativity, leadership and innovation towards the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047. The initiative began with the Viksit Bharat Quiz on 17 August 2026, which is open until 30 September 2026 on the MY Bharat platform. Under the flagship Viksit Bharat Challenge, participants progress through the Essay Challenge, District Championships and State/UT-level stages before culminating in the National Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue in New Delhi from 10–12 January 2027. Alongside this, VBYLD 2027 features five additional tracks—Cultural Track, Design for Bharat, Hack for Social Cause, Youth Entrepreneurs Challenge and Youth Parliament—providing platforms for young people to demonstrate their cultural talent, creative and design thinking, technology-led solutions, entrepreneurial ideas and leadership in parliamentary processes. Selected young participants across these tracks will get an opportunity to engage with policymakers and, at the national level, present their ideas before the Prime Minister.

The current MY Bharat ecosystem also hosts a range of youth-focused initiatives, including Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat, Viksit Vibrant Village Programme, Viksit Bharat Youth Parliament, Viksit Bharat Padyatra, Viksit Bharat Yuva Connect and Khelo India Dialogue, alongside Experiential Learning and volunteering opportunities.

Through the Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat campaign, MY Bharat is also contributing to the nationwide effort to mobilise young people for a healthier and drug-free India. The 100 Weeks Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan commenced with the Rashtriya Sankalp Samaroh in September 2026, with youth participation through pledge-taking, signature campaigns, creative activities and discussions across the country.

The 3 crore + milestone therefore represents more than an increase in registrations. It reflects the expanding scale of a national platform through which young Indians can learn through experience, participate in community initiatives, develop leadership capabilities and contribute their ideas to the country's development journey.

As MY Bharat continues to expand its digital and grassroots ecosystem, the platform remains focused on strengthening Yuva Shakti, Jan Bhagidari and youth-led nation-building, in keeping with the vision of empowering India's young population to contribute meaningfully towards a Viksit Bharat @2047.

Ministry of Road Transport & Highways

Minister of State for Corporate Affairs and Road Transport & Highways Shri Harsh Malhotra Lays Foundation Stones for Two Foot Over Bridges on Delhi-Saharanpur-Dehradun Expressway in East Delhi

FOBs Equipped with Lift Facilities to Enhance Pedestrian Safety, Accessibility and Mobility; Third FOB Approved near Bhajanpura, Garhi Mendu

23 SEP 2026 2:39PM by PIB Delhi

Shri Harsh Malhotra, Hon’ble Minister of State for Corporate Affairs and Road Transport and Highways and Member of Parliament, East Delhi Lok Sabha, today laid the foundation stones for two Foot Over Bridges (FOBs) at Geeta Colony/Gandhi Nagar (Km 5+100) and Ramesh Park, Laxmi Nagar (Km 2+800) on the Delhi-Saharanpur-Dehradun Expressway (NH-709B) in East Delhi.

The occasion was graced by Shri Arvinder Singh Lovely, MLA, Gandhi Nagar and Chairman, Trans Yamuna Development Board; Shri Abhay Verma, MLA, Laxmi Nagar and Chief Whip, Delhi Legislative Assembly; Dr. Anil Goyal, MLA, Krishna Nagar; local councillors and prominent citizens of the area.

The Minister said that the initiative reflects the vision of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi for modern, citizen-centric infrastructure that directly improves ease of living and safer mobility. He said that under his leadership and the guidance of Union Minister for Road Transport & Highways Shri Nitin Gadkari, India has witnessed rapid development of modern expressways, high-capacity road corridors and public safety initiatives.

Shri Harsh Malhotra stated that the initiative marks an important step towards enhancing pedestrian safety and improving everyday mobility for residents of East Delhi. He said that the Delhi section of the Expressway passes through densely populated areas and connects major residential, commercial and local movement corridors, making safe pedestrian infrastructure particularly important.

The FOBs will be equipped with lift facilities, providing safe, dedicated and convenient pedestrian crossings while reducing pedestrian-vehicle interaction and facilitating uninterrupted vehicular movement. The lifts will also improve accessibility for senior citizens, persons with mobility challenges, students, workers and other pedestrians.

In addition to the two FOBs, one more Foot Over Bridge has been approved at Km 10+800 near Bhajanpura, Garhi Mendu. The total cost of the three Foot Over Bridges will be ₹12.8 crore.

headline: TDB-DST backs India’s next-generation air mobility ambitions with ₹285 crore RDI support to Ubifly Technologies
fullText:
Ministry of Science & Technology

TDB-DST backs India’s next-generation air mobility ambitions with ₹285 crore RDI support to Ubifly Technologies

Support under the ₹1 lakh crore RDI Fund to take indigenous ePlane technology from TRL-6 to TRL-9

23 SEP 2026 2:27PM by PIB Delhi

India’s push to build a globally competitive, private-sector-led deep-tech ecosystem is gaining momentum with the Technology Development Board (TDB), Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India, approving ₹285 crore financial support to Ubifly Technologies Private Limited, Chennai under the Research Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund for advancing its indigenous ePlane Advanced Air Mobility Solution.

With a total approved project cost of ₹570 crore, the project will take the technology from Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 6 to TRL 9, marking a significant step towards the commercial deployment of an indigenous advanced air mobility platform. The TDB support will be provided through Optionally Convertible Debentures (OCD).

The e200X, being developed by Ubifly Technologies, is a three-seater, zero-emission advanced air mobility aircraft configured for one pilot and two passengers, with a targeted range of 110 km and an ideal speed of 160 kmph. The aircraft brings together multiple indigenous technology elements, including vertical rotors, forward propellers, proprietary flight-control algorithms, power-distribution controllers and battery-pack modules with integrated cooling systems. The company has also designed the complete airframe, including the fuselage, wings and booms, in-house.

A notable feature of the aircraft is its landing gear designed for both conventional and vertical landing, offering operational flexibility for advanced air mobility applications. Its compact architecture is intended to enable operations from relatively small spaces and facilitate multiple trips on a single battery charge. The project is categorised under Deep Technology, with Space Technologies as the sub-sector. Its advancement from TRL-6 to TRL-9 will involve further technology maturation, testing, validation and scale-up towards an operationally demonstrated system.

Sh. Rajesh Kumar Pathak, Secretary, TDB, said, “The RDI Fund represents a significant shift towards enabling private-sector participation in the development of high-impact technologies and taking promising innovations closer to deployment. TDB’s support to Ubilfy Technologies reflects the Government of India’s commitment to strengthening indigenous capabilities in deep technologies and creating pathways for Indian technologies to move from advanced development to commercialisation. The ePlane project brings together advanced electric propulsion, aerospace engineering and intelligent systems.”

Representative of Ubifly Technologies Private Limited said, “The support extended by TDB under the RDI Fund will provide important impetus to the continued development and validation of our ePlane technology. Taking the e200X from TRL-6 towards TRL-9 requires sustained investment in engineering, testing and technology maturation. We appreciate TDB’s support in enabling this transition and in strengthening indigenous advanced air mobility capabilities in India.”

He said that timely career progression is important for keeping employees motivated and ensuring effective functioning of the administration.

He said that while employees may have a range of demands, their genuine issues would be looked into through the appropriate mechanism. He also said that inputs received from employees on service and cadre-related matters are important and should continue to be brought before the concerned authorities.

The interaction was with representatives of the Central Secretariat Group-C Employees’ Association, representing more than 8,000 Group-C employees working across 135 Ministries, Departments and Organisations under the Central Secretariat. The delegation placed before the Minister a detailed set of concerns relating to service conditions and career progression of its members.

The representatives placed their inputs regarding cadre review and the existing cadre structure, seeking consideration of issues affecting promotional avenues and career progression. Dr. Jitendra Singh said that such genuine inputs would be considered through the appropriate institutional mechanism.

Under the guidance of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah, special attention to be given to field and outstation offices that interface directly with the public

Special Campaign 6 in MHA will focus on creating sustainable and environment-friendly workplaces, while simultaneously addressing pendency in various categories of references and matters

23 SEP 2026 1:16PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) is geared up to participate actively in Special Campaign 6, being organized by the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG). The Campaign will be undertaken in two phases:

1. Preparation Phase: 15 September to 30 September 2026

2. Implementation Phase: 2 October to 31 October 2026

Inspired by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision to institutionalize Swachhata and minimize pendency in Government the campaign aimed at promoting cleanliness, streamlining work, addressing pending grievances. Under the guidance of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah, special attention to be given to field and outstation offices that interface directly with the public.

The Special Campaign 6 in the Ministry of Home Affairs will focus on creating sustainable and environment-friendly workplaces, while simultaneously addressing pendency in various categories of references and matters. These include references from Members of Parliament, references from State Governments, Parliament Assurances, Inter-Ministerial Consultations, Public Grievances and Appeals, as well as improved record management.

The implementation of Special Campaign 6 is being monitored at the highest level in the Ministry. The Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) and Central Police Organizations (CPOs) have been sensitized about the importance of the Campaign and have been encouraged to make concerted efforts and go the extra mile to achieve the objectives and targets identified under the Campaign.

The Ministry remains committed to institutionalizing the gains of the Special Campaign through sustained efforts towards cleanliness, efficient record management, timely disposal of pending matters and creation of cleaner, greener and more productive workplaces.

The Ministry of Home Affairs and its attached/subordinate organizations have been actively participating in the Special Campaign for reducing pendency and promoting cleanliness and efficient record management. During the period from November 2025 to August 2026, the Ministry and its field/outstation offices made significant progress in the disposal of pending matters and creation of a cleaner and more efficient workplace.

The key achievements during the period are as follows:

761 Swachhta campaigns were conducted at various locations by the Ministry, including its field and outstation offices.

299 references from Members of Parliament, 336 references from State Governments and 7 PMO references were disposed of.

A total of 52,050 Public Grievances and 7,410 Public Grievance Appeals received during the period were disposed of by the Ministry.

1,02,084 sq. ft. of office space was freed in the offices of MHA and the Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs).

To facilitate smooth collation of data and ensure its accuracy, the Ministry of Home Affairs has been utilizing an intra-Ministry portal through which all Divisions of the Ministry, as well as the Union Territories and Delhi Police, upload campaign-related data. The portal has enabled effective coordination with various Divisions and offices and has facilitated timely collection and consolidation of accurate data.

Ministry of Textiles to Undertake Special Campaign 6 with Focus on Swachhata, Pendency and E-waste Management

23 SEP 2026 12:26PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India has announced Special Campaign 6, which will run from 2nd October to 31st October 2026, with a focus on Swachhta (cleanliness) and reducing pendency in government activities.

The main goal of this yearly campaign is to make cleanliness a permanent habit in government offices and quickly finish all pending official work.

The Three Key Phases of the Campaign:

Preparatory Phase (September 15th –30th, 2026): This phase has already started. Ministries will use this time to identify targets (pending references from MP’s, State Governments, Inter-Ministerial references (Cabinet Notes), PMO, Parliamentary Assurances pending for more than 3 months, Public Grievances and Appeals),Record Management – Review of files/recording and weeding of files/closing of e-files, find pending files, and locate scrap materials for disposal.

Implementation Phase (October 2nd –31st, 2026): During this month-long phase, offices will actively clean up spaces, dispose of waste, and resolve pending files.

Evaluation Phase (November 16th –30th, 2026): In this final phase, the overall work done and results achieved across all ministries will be reviewed and measured.

The Campaign this year will emphasize “Effective Collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste.

This year focus on scientific disposal/management of e-waste generated in Government offices and the main phase will be the action phase, during which all out efforts shall be made to achieve the targets identified in preparatory phase information shall be provided on monitoring portal on daily basis by a dedicated portal https://scdpm.nic.in/specialcampaign6/.

Achievements and Best Practices of Special Campaign 5

Special Campaign 6 builds upon the achievements of Special Campaign 5 to further the objective of improving the experience of citizens with government offices. During Special Campaign 5, the Ministry of Textiles conducted a comprehensive review of 19,376 physical files was conducted. As a result, 6264 physical files were weeded out, and 274 e-files were closed. This diligent review process led to the freeing up of 25498 square feet of space. Revenue amounting to Rs. 11.35 Lakh was generated from the disposal of scrap and other redundant materials. A total of 200 sites were successfully cleaned during the campaign.

It is also important to note that 63 VIP references were promptly addressed and resolved. Furthermore, regarding the Public Grievances pending at the start of the campaign, the Ministry achieved 100% of its target by redressing 44 Public Grievances.

The Ministry of Textiles is dedicated to advancing the goals and successes of previous campaigns. We will put forward the same level of dedication and collective effort to make Special Campaign 6 equally successful.

headline: DRI seizes around 21 kg foreign-origin gold worth Rs. 32 crore in crackdown on gold smuggling
fullText:
Ministry of Finance

DRI seizes around 21 kg foreign-origin gold worth Rs. 32 crore in crackdown on gold smuggling

Seized gold smuggled from neighbouring countries; 5 persons arrested

23 SEP 2026 9:13PM by PIB Delhi

Continuing its sustained crackdown on gold smuggling, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has seized around 21 kg foreign-origin gold in two operations, cumulatively valued at more than Rs. 61 crore in seven separate operations carried out across the country. Five persons have been arrested under the provisions of the Customs Act, 1962.

Based on specific intelligence, DRI officers intercepted two new Thar vehicles near Palwal Toll Plaza. The very ingenious and sophisticated concealed cavity in the chassis of both the vehicles that had been created by removing and expertly welding back a portion of the chassis over the rear wheel proved extremely difficult to detect. Only upon painstaking rummaging of these vehicles, DRI officers could successfully locate the concealment. A total of 15.18 kg. gold in form of bars, valued at approximately Rs. 23.30 crore was recovered from two vehicles and seized on 19.09.26. Four persons accompanying the vehicles were arrested. The intelligence indicates that the gold has been smuggled from Myanmar.

Earlier, in another operation on 16.09.26, officers of DRI intercepted a passenger at Jewar Toll Plaza, who was travelling by bus from Gorakhpur towards Delhi. Personal search led to the recovery and seizure of 5.8 kg of foreign-origin gold, comprising five 1-kg gold bars and approximately 800 grams of cut pieces, valued concealed in a specially designed cotton waist belt. The person was arrested under the Customs Act, 1962. Preliminary investigation indicated that the gold had been handed over to him in Kathmandu and brought into India through the India-Nepal land border.

In last three weeks, DRI officers have seized around 123 kg gold and around 10 kg silver, collectively valued at more than Rs 187 crore in various operations across the country. 58 persons have been arrested for smuggling gold. These operations underscore DRI’s continued focus on disrupting organised gold-smuggling networks and detecting increasingly sophisticated methods of concealment.

headline: DRI seizes around 12 kg foreign-origin gold smuggled from Bangladesh worth Rs. 17 crore in a crackdown on cross border gold smuggling

Subsequently, DRI joined the recovered gold, the same was seized under the provisions of Section 110 of the Customs Act, 1962. Previously, on 10-11.09.26, foreign-origin gold comprising of 48 bars, weighing around 5.9 kg was recovered near the India-Bangladesh border fence in the BOP Pathergata area by BSF personnel, which was also taken over and seized by DRI.

In Patna, DRI officers, recovered and seized 15 gold bars and 4 tiny cut pieces of gold of foreign origin weighing around 1.71 kg from a train passenger. The gold was concealed in cloth knee cap wrapped around both his legs. The investigations indicated that the gold had been smuggled from Bangladesh. The person has been arrested.

The operations highlight the continued efforts of DRI done in close coordination with BSF to disrupt the networks involved in the smuggling, transportation and distribution of foreign-origin gold through the Bangladesh route.

headline: Union Minister for Finance & Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman inaugurates BRICS Heads of Tax Authorities Meeting in New Delhi
fullText:
Ministry of Finance

Union Minister for Finance & Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman inaugurates BRICS Heads of Tax Authorities Meeting in New Delhi

India’s BRICS Tax Chairship delivers landmark outcomes across technology, administration and people

Two new India-led Working Groups on International Taxation and Revenue Statistics formally established; BRICS Tax Progress Report 2026 adopted

23 SEP 2026 8:38PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Finance & Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman inaugurated the BRICS Heads of Tax Authorities Meeting in New Delhi today, as the culmination of India’s BRICS Chairship of the tax cooperation track. The meeting was also addressed by the Union Finance Minister, Union Minister of State for Finance Shri Pankaj Chaudhary, and Revenue Secretary Shri Arvind Shrivastava.

The meeting was attended by Shri Ravi Agrawal, Chairman, CBDT, Shri Prasenjit Singh, Member (Legislation), CBDT, other Members of CBDT, and senior officers of the Department of Revenue (DoR). The meeting, hosted by the Central Board of Direct Taxes, Ministry of Finance, Government of India, brought together the Heads of Tax Authorities of the BRICS member countries. Representatives from ten BRICS tax administrations - Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, India, Indonesia, Iran, Russia, South Africa, and the United Arab Emirates - came together at one place to share their experiences and discuss emerging challenges through cooperation and collaboration.

In her address on the occasion, Smt. Sitharaman highlighted technology, administration and people as the three recurring themes of BRICS tax cooperation during India’s Chairship. She emphasised the role of data and digital infrastructure in making tax administration more precise and accessible, the importance of durable institutional mechanisms and practical tools that can sustain cooperation beyond individual Chairships, and the value of investing in people and building professional relationships across tax administrations. She also underscored that the perspectives of BRICS economies are essential to ensuring the fairness and durability of ongoing multilateral tax negotiations, including the negotiations on the UN Framework Convention on International Tax Cooperation.

The meeting formally adopted several landmark outcomes. Two new Working Groups on International Taxation and Transfer Pricing, and on Revenue Statistics, were established. Both will be led by India, creating sustained institutional platforms that will continue regardless of the Chairship. The first-ever in-person BRICS Young Tax Professionals Capacity Building Programme, held at the National Academy of Direct Taxes, Nagpur in April 2026, was institutionalised as an annual feature of BRICS tax cooperation. The BRICS Tax Cross-Learning Lab was formally launched, integrating the work of the Client-Centric Administration and HR Practices Working Groups into a joint peer-learning platform. The Terms of Reference of the BRICS Tax Support Network was also approved.

The meeting concluded with the formal signing of the BRICS Tax Progress Report 2026, the complete record of India’s Chairship of the BRICS Tax track. The People’s Republic of China was welcomed as the incoming Chair of the BRICS tax cooperation track for 2027.

The Heads of Tax Authorities lauded the Government of India for the successful organisation of the meeting and for the quality and depth of India’s Chairship of the BRICS tax track.

headline: DRI seizes 10,000 kg of firecrackers worth Rs. 3 crore at Nhava Sheva port
fullText:

DRI seizes 10,000 kg of firecrackers worth Rs. 3 crore at Nhava Sheva port

Firecrackers concealed behind declared cargo of bottles; key syndicate member arrested

23 SEP 2026 8:07PM by PIB Delhi

In an intelligence led operation, officers of DRI, intercepted an import consignment at Nhava Sheva Port suspected to contain firecrackers and on examination of the same found firecrackers concealed under the guise of declared goods, namely “Bottle & Wallpaper.”

Seized firecracker 288 Gatling

The detailed examination led to recovery of 19,800 pieces of firecrackers (known as 288 Gatling), weighing approximately 10,000 Kg with a market value of about Rs. 3 crore. Except for the first three rows containing the declared goods, the container was found to be filled predominantly with firecrackers. The firecrackers, along with the declared cover cargo, were seized under the provisions of the Customs Act, 1962.

The import of firecrackers is 'Restricted' under the Foreign Trade Policy and requires valid authorisation from DGFT, and requisite license from the Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organization (PESO) under the Explosives Rules, 2008.

During the course of investigation, the key syndicate member, who was orchestrating and attempting the clandestine clearance of the said goods, has been arrested under the Customs Act, 1962.

The operation underscores DRI’s continued focus on detecting misdeclaration and clandestine import of restricted goods through commercial cargo channels.

headline: Bihar’s Heritage, Folk Traditions and Spiritual Legacy Reflects in 65 PM Mementos
fullText:
Ministry of Culture

Bihar’s Heritage, Folk Traditions and Spiritual Legacy Reflects in 65 PM Mementos

Collection brings together Madhubani and Manjusha art, Sikki craft, historical figures and commemorative artefacts

23 SEP 2026 7:47PM by PIB Delhi

The cultural richness of Bihar finds expression in a collection of 65 mementos featured in the PM Mementos e-Auction 2026, bringing together the State’s diverse traditions of folk art, handcraft, spirituality, history and heritage. The collection ranges from intricate Madhubani paintings and Sikki craft to representations of revered temples, historical personalities and national symbols.

Rather than representing a single tradition, the collection offers glimpses into the many cultural identities associated with Bihar.

Madhubani and Mithila traditions

A significant part of the collection is devoted to the celebrated Mithila/Madhubani painting tradition. The mementos include depictions of Ram Sita Vivah, Ram Darbar, Chhath Puja, Das Mahavidya and sacred Yantras, along with a Kachni-style Madhubani artwork depicting the Ramayana.

The collection also features several Mithila Paags, hand-painted with traditional motifs such as fish and lotus flowers. The Paag, a distinctive headgear of the Mithila region, is represented through multiple designs and forms.

Craft traditions rooted in the region

Bihar’s craft heritage is also represented through Sikki grass art, including a detailed model of the New Parliament House of India and a traditional woven Sikki basket with integrated coasters. A hand-painted Madhubani artwork on a bamboo winnowing basket combines folk painting with traditional utility craft.

Another distinctive piece is a Manjusha (Angika) painting from Bhagalpur, depicting Bharat Mata against the map of India. Executed in the traditional three-colour palette of yellow, green and red, the work reflects the storytelling tradition of Manjusha art.

History and spiritual heritage

The collection also traverses Bihar’s historical and spiritual landscape. A copper-plate memento depicting Mangal Pandey commemorates the freedom fighter associated with the First War of Independence of 1857. Other artefacts include representations of Ashoka Stambh, Takhat Sri Harmandir Ji Patna Sahib, Lord Buddha, Mahavir Swami and various temples and pilgrimage sites across the State.

Among the religious landmarks featured are Chandika Sthan and Badi Durga Maharani of Munger, Punaura Dham in Sitamarhi, Maa Aranya Devi Temple in Bhojpur, Baba Garibnath Temple in Muzaffarpur, Gorakhnath Dham and Mundeshwari Devi Temple in Kaimur.

The collection further includes mementos associated with Jan Nayak Karpoori Thakur, Acharya Chanakya and Guru Valmiki, alongside representations of the Ramayana and other cultural traditions.

With base prices ranging from ₹1,500 to ₹1,20,000, the Bihar collection offers collectors an opportunity to engage with the State’s living traditions of art, craft, faith and history through mementos presented to the Prime Minister.

The 8th edition of the PM Mementos e-Auction is live online till October 2, 2026. For auction dates, participation details and the complete catalogue, refer to the official PM Mementos e-Auction portal at: https://pmmementos.gov.in/#/

The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, will undertake Special Campaign 6.0 from 2nd to 31st October 2026, with a focus on institutionalising Swachhata, reducing pendency, strengthening record management, promoting responsible e-waste disposal and ensuring optimum utilisation of office space across the Department and its attached, subordinate and autonomous organisations.

The campaign will be implemented in two phases. The Preparatory Phase, being undertaken from 15th to 30th September 2026, focuses on identification of targets, review of records and pending references, and preparations for cleanliness drives and disposal activities during the main campaign period.

Special Campaign 6.0 aims to achieve saturation of Swachhata across the office premises of DPIIT and its attached, subordinate and autonomous organisations, including their field and branch offices located across the country. The campaign will cover all 19 attached, subordinate and autonomous organisations under the administrative control of DPIIT.

DPIIT had participated extensively in Special Campaign 5.0 and achieved significant outcomes in cleanliness, record management, pendency reduction and space utilisation. During the campaign, 1,572 physical files were reviewed, of which 1,119 files were weeded out in accordance with applicable record-retention procedures. Disposal of obsolete records and scrap resulted in the release of 11,235 square feet of office space and revenue generation of ₹17,69,569.

The Department also addressed its identified pendency targets, including disposal of Public Grievances and Public Grievance Appeals, as well as identified areas for simplification of rules and procedures. These initiatives contributed to improving efficiency, responsiveness and the overall work experience of officials and staff.

Building on these outcomes, Special Campaign 6.0 will place greater emphasis on sustainable cleanliness practices, systematic record management and efficient utilisation of government office space. The key areas of focus will include saturation of Swachhata in office premises and surrounding areas; identification and disposal of pending references within prescribed timelines; review and weeding out of records as per applicable record-retention schedules; effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste through authorised channels; disposal of obsolete and unserviceable items and scrap; optimum utilisation and release of office space; improvement of workplace aesthetics, cleanliness and functionality; and institutionalisation of sustainable and environmentally responsible practices.

A special thrust will be given to e-waste management, with emphasis on the proper identification, segregation, collection and disposal of electronic and electrical waste through authorised agencies. This will facilitate environmentally sound disposal of obsolete electronic equipment while supporting cleaner and better-organised government workplaces.

The campaign will also encourage DPIIT's organisations to adopt innovative and replicable solutions that promote sustainability and the principles of a circular economy. An example in this regard is the “Waste to Wealth” initiative undertaken by the Indian Rubber Material Research Institute (IRMRI), an autonomous organisation under DPIIT. Under the initiative, discarded rubber scrap was utilised for construction of a road section and access road using Waste Rubber Tiles and Crumb Rubber Cement Concrete (CRCC), incorporating approximately 10–15 per cent waste rubber particles in the cement-concrete mix. The performance of the road was scientifically monitored for parameters including strength, elasticity and durability.

Such innovative practices will be encouraged during Special Campaign 6.0 for wider adoption and replication, wherever feasible.

Through Special Campaign 6.0, DPIIT and its organisations will make concerted efforts to further strengthen the culture of Swachhata, efficiency, accountability and good governance across their offices. The campaign will also seek to ensure that the outcomes achieved are sustained and institutionalised beyond the campaign period, contributing to cleaner, more efficient, sustainable and citizen-centric government workplaces.

Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs Celebrated 11th Ayurveda Day with Focal Theme "Ayurveda for a Healthier Tomorrow on 23rd September, 2026"

23 SEP 2026 6:54PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) celebrated the 11th Ayurveda Day on 23.09.2026 at Sankalp Bhawan, New Delhi, aligning with the nationwide celebrations spearheaded by the Ministry of Ayush. The event was centered around the theme, "Ayurveda for a Healthier Tomorrow," focusing on preventive healthcare, wellness and sustainable lifestyle practices.

To mark this significant occasion, MoHUA organized a specialized seminar, discourse and an interactive session at Sankalp Bhawan. Shri R.K. Tiwary, ADG, Urban Health Services (UHS), MoHUA delivered a brief lecture around the theme. The expert lecture on Scientific pathways for prevention, integration, community wellbeing and One Health was delivered by Dr. Ramavtar Sharma, Associate Professor & Head of Department of Swathavritta (Preventive and Social Medicine), All India Institute of Ayurveda, New Delhi and a lecture on Medicinal plants and Ayurveda by Dr. Ashish Kumar Tripathi, Domain Expert and Editor (JDRAS) from the Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS), Ministry of Ayush.

The program saw active participation from senior officers and staff members of the Ministry. In this regard, and in view of the changing global health landscape, the session highlighted a critical shift from episodic treatment to prevention-led, whole-system health. Highlighting that lifestyle-linked conditions and mind-body stress are core determinants of modern health, the speakers emphasized that tomorrow’s healthcare must proactively protect community wellbeing. Dr. Ramavtar Sharma detailed how small, measurable and repeatable self-care modules—such as Workplace Yoga, posture correction, eye-breaks, and movement protocols—can be practically embedded into daily office routines to naturally improve adherence, vitality, and functional productivity.

Complementing this public-health framework, Dr. Ashish Kumar Tripathi expanded upon "Nature's Pharmacy: Tradition, Science and Healing," introducing the audience to the therapeutic potentials of medicinal plants. He detailed the scientific dynamics of daily wellness protocols (Dinacharya) and seasonal adaptations (Ritucharya) required to balance metabolic health and build long-term respiratory and immune resilience against modern environmental stress.

During the interactive session, ministry officials engaged with the experts on seamlessly adopting these scalable preventive strategies into urban administrative frameworks.
